subject: Audit / Access log location, exportability, and deletion workflow
messages:
From: security@firmwave.com
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-27T09:12:00+00:00
Subject: Clarify where audit/access logs live and how we can export them

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. Before we move forward with the POC, our compliance team needs written confirmation on a few things about Redwood's audit and access logs for accounts that elect EU residency. Please can you confirm the following in writing: 

1) For the EU residency option, where are audit logs stored (region/zone and provider level)? Is data encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys?
2) What are the default retention periods you enforce for:
   - Admin/audit logs (who changed what)
   - Access logs (api requests, IPs, agent ids)
   - Runtime token/session traces (short-lived request traces)
3) For exports: can we trigger an on-demand export of the last N months of logs to our S3 (eu-west-1) bucket? What formats do you support (NDJSON, CSV, gzipped JSON)? Any compression/partitioning guarantees?
4) Deletion: if FirmWave requests deletion of logs for a subset of user IDs, what is the workflow and SLA to fully purge those records (including backups and snapshots)? Is there a legal-hold option to suspend deletion for an investigation?

I've attached our short questionnaire (FirmWave_Retention_Qs.pdf). If you can provide an example export field list and a sample file, that would be ideal.

Cheers,
Lina Costa
Senior Compliance Manager, FirmWave
security@firmwave.com

[attachment: FirmWave_Retention_Qs.pdf (pdf)]

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: security@firmwave.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-27T10:03:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Clarify where audit/access logs live and how we can export them

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers; I also attached a small NDJSON sample showing the typical field set. I'm happy to hop on a quick call to walk through anything.

Short answers: 
- EU residency: logs are stored in the selected region (we currently support eu-west-1 and eu-central-1). Under the Private/EU residency option we pin both primary storage and backups to EU regions; provider is AWS for those regions. Data at rest is encrypted and you can opt into a customer-managed KMS key (CMK) for the account.

- Default retention (configurable per account):
  * Admin / audit logs (configuration changes, role changes): default 2 years, can be shortened to 90 days or extended up to 7 years by contract.
  * Access logs (API request metadata: timestamp, endpoint, status, client IP): default 13 months (to align with some regulatory requests), configurable to 90 days—7 years based on plan.
  * Runtime traces (short, high-volume request traces/KV cache traces): default 30 days; high-volume traces are sampled and can be exported for longer-term storage.

- Exports: we support on-demand exports to customer S3 (eu-west-1) or SFTP. Supported formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON), gzipped CSV, and Parquet for larger volumes. Exports are partitioned by day and hour, and we guarantee a manifest file with checksums. For your requested N-month export we can do a one-off bulk export; typical throughput and time-to-completion depends on the window (we'll provide an estimate when you pick dates). There is an egress charge for large exports; we'll include that in the export request confirmation.

- Deletion workflow: for targeted deletions by user ID we have a two-phase process:
  1) A soft-delete flag is applied within 24 hours (no surface-level user data accessible).
  2) A background purge job removes the flagged records from primary stores and secondary indexes within a 30-day SLA unless under legal hold. Backups/snapshots containing that data are retained for the snapshot retention window (generally 90 days for EU residency default) and are subject to the same purge process during scheduled snapshot compaction cycles — full physical removal can take up to the snapshot retention period. If you need immediate cryptographic erasure from backups we offer an accelerated purge option under contract.

- Legal hold: yes, accounts can request a legal hold which freezes deletion for specified identifiers; we maintain a ledger of holds and keep exports immutable until released.

Attachments: requested_field_sample.ndjson (example lines, anonymized). Let me know if you want the full export into your bucket and the date range.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Security Liaison
Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

[attachment: requested_field_sample.ndjson (ndjson)]

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: security@firmwave.com
Date: 2027-05-27T13:18:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Clarify where audit/access logs live and how we can export them

Adding a few technical clarifications for Lina so the export/ingest team can plan: 

- Field set (example): event_time (ISO8601), tenant_id, user_id (pseudonymized by default on exports if requested), endpoint, http_method, status_code, request_id, upstream_model_id, latency_ms, client_ip (masked on EU export by default), user_agent, trace_id, bytes_sent. We can include full JWT payloads only under an elevated access request.

- Export partitioning: daily folders with hourly shards (e.g., s3://firmwave-exports/YYYY/MM/DD/HH/part-*.ndjson.gz). We also publish _SUCCESS and manifest.json for each day.

- Pseudonymization: we support on-the-fly hashing of user identifiers with a salt you provide (deterministic per-account) so your internal systems can join datasets while keeping direct PII masked.

- Deletion+backups note: because snapshots are immutable for the snapshot window, if FirmWave needs absolute deletion sooner than the snapshot retention you must request the accelerated purge add-on; this schedules a re-encryption / key-rotation + re-compaction which is contract-level.

If FirmWave wants me to open the export job I can trigger it; please confirm target bucket, IAM role (or presigned URL method), date range and whether you need pseudonymization.

- Aditya (Infra Eng, Redwood)

From: security@firmwave.com
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, legal@firmwave.com
Date: 2027-05-27T15:46:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Clarify where audit/access logs live and how we can export them

Hi Sofia / Aditya — this is very helpful, thanks. A few follow-ups (short):

1) We'll take the EU residency option and want eu-central-1 as the region. Please confirm you support CMKs in eu-central-1 (yes/no).
2) For the POC let's export the last 3 months of access logs and a 12-month slice of admin/audit logs. Target bucket: s3://firmwave-compliance-exports (we will provide an IAM role).
3) Please pseudonymize user_id with a salt we will provide. We do not need full JWT payloads.
4) Legal hold: we will likely use holds during the POC for a subset of users; please add the legal-hold process to the export job request so we understand implications.

If you can send the export job initiation form and a short estimate of hours-to-complete + egress estimate, we'll route this internally and provide the IAM role. Also attaching our signed questionnaire (FirmWave_Retention_Qs.pdf).

Best,
Lina Costa
Senior Compliance Manager, FirmWave
